summary: Langfuse now holds the traces with a model call in them; message-ingest reporting moved to metrics.
details: Every ambient message was opening a Langfuse trace, and none of them contain a model call — six deterministic stages, a database row, a memory feed. Because ingest is the busiest thing Nora does, that was 97 of the last 100 traces on the live deployment, across 12 rooms she is not even allowlisted for, which left the collector unreadable for the turns that matter.

A trace now reaches Langfuse when the work under it can contain a generation. That keeps the tag turn and the reflection fold — including a tag refused before it ever reaches the model, whose trace is the one that says why — and drops the ingest family.

Nothing measured was lost, only moved to where it belongs: every ambient message still reports how its ingest ended, on a counter labelled by platform, room type and outcome. The other facts the trace carried were already counted (unmapped senders, attachment custody, both refusal counters, and the engagement gate's own error series).

The decision is per entry point, not per span, so the stages inside a real turn still show up as its children — that is what makes a turn ending early end visibly at a named stage rather than as a trace with a hole in it.
limitations: An individual ambient message can no longer be inspected in Langfuse. Its outcome is on the metrics endpoint, and the room id is still written to the host log when a message is refused. Restoring the trace for a plumbing entry point is a one-attribute change if a case for it appears.
